findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: A finitely generated Z_p-module generally has torsion, so X(\tilde{k})_{Gal(\tilde{k}/k)} is isomorphic to Z_p^r \oplus T where T is a finite p-group. If T \neq 0 or r = 0 with T \neq 0, it is not a free Z_p-module and does not have a Z_p-basis; moreover, it has not been proven that X(\tilde{k})_{Gal(\tilde{k}/k)} is torsion-free or free over Z_p, rendering the subsequent basis and matrix representation arguments invalid in general without justification or modification (e.g. passing to Z/pZ or modulo torsion). Exactly as the screening note states, the proof assumes without justification that the coinvariant module is a free Z_p-module of finite rank, admitting a basis and a direct sum complement in this form without addressing possible torsion components in X(\tilde{k})_{Gal(\tilde{k}/k)}.

evidence.text: Now, assume that \( X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} \) is not trivial, i.e., \( C \neq \tilde{k} \). Since \( C/k \) is Galois, so is \( C/k_{\text{cyc}} \). Hence, since \( C/N \) is abelian, we can regard \( \operatorname{Gal}(C/N) \) as a \( \operatorname{Gal}(N/k_{\text{cyc}}) \)-module by Lemma 2.1.2, and we can regard \( X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} \) as its \( \operatorname{Gal}(N/k_{\text{cyc}}) \)-submodule with trivial action. Since the free \( \mathbb{Z}_p \)-module \( \operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/N) \simeq \mathbb{Z}_p^{\oplus 2} \) is projective, \( X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} \) is non-trivial and a direct summand of \( \operatorname{Gal}(C/N) \) as a \( \mathbb{Z}_p \)-module. Therefore, we can take a \( \mathbb{Z}_p \)-basis \( \{ g_1, \ldots, g_m \} \) of \( \operatorname{Gal}(C/N) \) such that \( \{ g_1, \ldots, g_{m-2} \} \) becomes a \( \mathbb{Z}_p \)-basis of \( X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} \).
